issues.cell: Strips, zones and nearest points (adj l. 350–359); the bent-group sentence's strip, lawful crossing and (i)–(ii) (adj l. 483–500); No gate and no tower (adj l. 455–466); the fixed-place sentence (adj l. 519–528)
issues.claim: Every rule is stated for one raised way ('inside the raised way's strip', 'meeting the deck line once', 'the nearer of the two points clear of it'). Nothing rules two standing raised ways whose under-deck strips, fixed-place zones or held buildings' widened strips meet or lie within a band's width at one wall (no rule anywhere in the set; base l. 2537 and V06 l. 2815 only keep supports off each other). A tower, gate, fixed place or bent-group line moved clear of A's strip may land in B's and be moved back (no end) or on (a union); (i)'s nearest lawful crossing of A may meet B's deck line at a support; 'the two points' presumes one crossing of the line. Builders differ; one reading need not terminate.
issues.required_change: Strips, zones and nearest points adds a 'Several raised ways' sentence: where strips, zones or held buildings' widened strips of two or more standing raised ways meet or lie within the wall's band's width along a wall's line, every rule reads their union as one strip (zone); the bent group's strip is the union, its lawful crossing meets each deck line once by that raised way's own lawful crossing, (i)'s nearest lawful crossing being the nearest lawful for every deck line of the union; a line crossing a strip or zone more than once or ending inside it takes, for each part, the nearest point clear along the line in either direction. 'the nearer of the two points clear of it' -> 'the nearest point clear of it'. Scope's E-S4 adds a two-raised-way ring fixture (epoch circuit and hand drawWall).

issues.cell: Strips, zones and nearest points (adj l. 355–359); No gate and no tower (adj l. 455–466); over the band (adj l. 367–371); the bent group's (iv) and strip (adj l. 484–486, 503–505); W2 and W13 cells (adj l. 589, 600); E-D3 (adj l. 1209, 1214); W6·C2 (adj l. 593)
issues.claim: Line and band made the band count for a line, but towers and gates are moved as points ('to the nearest point clear of a strip ... the nearer of the two points'): a tower or gatehouse is a footprint (base l. 7705–7706, 7742–7748); one builder stands its centre at the strip's edge, half its footprint under the deck (strip = deck plan + 1 m), uncapped (the cap caps the run's top and walk only), passing T-V6-47's '0 gates or towers in an under-deck strip' by station; another clears the footprint. And (iv) moves 'a gate inside the strip' — the bent group's strip widened by the band's half and held buildings' widened strips — while No gate and no tower, W2's last cell, W13 and E-D3's cause clear the under-deck strip only (E-D3's outcome says 'inside the strip').
issues.required_change: Strips, zones and nearest points adds: 'A tower or a gate is in a strip or zone when its footprint — the tower's, or the gatehouse's with its passage (§4.8; S10's step (0)) — meets it, and the nearest point clear of it is the nearest station on its line at which that footprint meets it no more; every bar that counts gates or towers in an under-deck strip counts their footprints.' (iv): 'a gate inside the strip by beneath's No gate and no tower' -> 'a gate whose footprint meets the under-deck strip (not the widened strip above) by ...'; E-D3: 'inside the strip' -> 'inside the under-deck strip'; the sweep's closing words 'no gate or tower in the under-deck strip' -> 'no gate's or tower's footprint in the under-deck strip'.

issues.cell: The fixed-place sentence (adj l. 514–528); Strips, zones and nearest points (adj l. 356–357); the bent group's (iii) (adj l. 503); E-P4 (adj l. 1155–1158); R7-03 (a) (adj l. 739–741); VEW-r6-03's weld case
issues.claim: Three mechanisms for one case: the fixed-place sentence and Strips, zones move 'a weld vertex along the bailey's outer arc' with a tie; E-P4 makes it a hard siting filter that moves nothing; the base pins weld vertices ('never move', base l. 7775–7777; S3 (8)–(9), base l. 5586–5593; §5.3 l. 9301). Sliding a weld vertex makes a non-vertex off the boundary; filtering re-sites the castle; neither says what follows when every candidate fails. The castle's law also fixes its town-side gate at the side's midpoint (base l. 5588–5590) and its vertex towers (base l. 7756), which the sentence omits: S3 (8) checks weld vertices only, so No gate and no tower moves them off their pinned places or the castle's law keeps them. VEW-r6-03's weld closure keeps two readings.
issues.required_change: Fixed places add 'every castle's town-side gate and the towers at its bailey's vertices'; 'a castle sited after the raised way its weld vertices along the bailey's outer arc (...)' -> 'a castle sited after the raised way is sited, never reshaped: §4.2 S3 (8)'s hard filter rejects a claim whose weld vertices, town-side gate or vertex towers would lie in a standing raised way's fixed-place zone, none of them ever moved (F-CASTLE's pinned vertices), the next candidate taken, then F-CASTLE's re-site rung, else kept inside (reported)'; delete 'a weld vertex along the bailey's outer arc' from Strips, zones; (iii) 'an anchor or weld vertex so moved' -> 'an anchor so moved'; E-P4 names the town-side gate and vertex towers; E-S3 adds a regeneration re-site fixture.

issues.cell: down before the wall's gate by path (adj l. 382–389, amended PRB7-06) × the way-and-channel table's row (d) (adj l. 625) and lead (adj l. 605–606)
issues.claim: At an epoch a priced deck's route crosses 'at a gate standing in that trace (an epoch's growth crossing at gates alone ...)'. An epoch grows a new stage through S5–S13 (V06 l. 1009), so S5b runs, and row (d) — on every path, an epoch among them — makes S5b's spawned primary 'a main gate' so the stage reaches N_k. At a new walled stage nothing stands in the picked boundary (S5a lays the trace after S5b, base l. 5049): the amended clause re-routes or drops the primary's deck, row (d) makes its gate. The parenthesis is §5.3's S5c legality (base l. 9287), which a spawned primary is not.
issues.required_change: 'at an epoch, and at a regeneration under a held trace, a gate standing in that trace (...)' -> 'at an epoch across a trace that stood before the epoch's growth step, and at a regeneration under a held trace, a gate standing in that trace (an epoch's growth crossing standing traces at gates alone, §5.3; a held wall's gates its own), the route solved to one of them; across the picked boundary of an epoch's new walled stage, the main gate its S5b gives a spawned primary (row (d))'. Scope's E-S2 adds an epoch walled-stage fixture: deck down before the picked boundary, the primary's main gate on ground part 0, gates exactly N_k.

issues.cell: A held building in an arch vault (adj l. 444–455) × C13 (adj l. 560–567); the lock sentence's 'Buildings ... stay held' (adj l. 339–341); veto 12
issues.claim: The held building 'holds its span against every wall' and every rule makes the wall give way; nothing rules the raised way's own op (C13: a hand re-shape, Arch spacing or Deck height) carrying that span (its key kept within p/2, base l. 2554–2556) over a standing band or wall strip: it then reads open (adj l. 429–433) and V04 removes the chamber with its door, links and accesses (V04 l. 1713–1716), unseating the declared placement (V04 l. 1722–1726). Builders: proceed (a held building reshaped — J144's 'Buildings ... stay held as before'), bend (item 101 R2), or refuse (refuse.locked or refuse.raised.meeting). No bar seats a building in a clause whose event edits the raised way.
issues.required_change: A held building in an arch vault adds: 'The raised way's own op gives way to it too: a hand re-shape, Arch spacing or Deck height edit (C13) that would bring a standing wall's band or wall strips over that span's under-deck strip is bent by the support step to the nearest course or value that keeps the span and its widened strip clear of every standing wall (item 101 R2), else refused by §7.1's lock row (refuse.locked, the building the blocking entity).' C13 adds 'a held building in an arch vault kept as beneath says'. Scope's E-S4 adds the re-shape fixture (bent; with no course, refused naming the building).

issues.cell: C10 (adj l. 554–557, amended PRB7-14) × down before the wall by hand (adj l. 392–397); Strips, zones (adj l. 353–354); veto 14; W1·C10 – W14·C10
issues.claim: C10 makes a hand repair of a dismantled span or cleared support 'that part's creation, C1'. For a road deck C1 is down before the wall: a course across a standing trace comes down before it, else refuse.raised.meeting. A viaduct span over a trace laid after it, dismantled (the engine never rebuilds one, V06 l. 726), lies between two standing piers at deck level and cannot come down, so every such repair is refused — against V06's 'rebuilt as a new span' (V06 l. 726, 3553) and the amended promise that 'a span or support repairRaised raises again stands over none of them'. Two outcomes; no bar (the sweep's C10 repairs a ruined span only).
issues.required_change: C10: '... being that part's creation, C1' -> '... being that part's creation, C1 — save that a road deck's new part, laid on its way's line between its standing parts, spans a trace laid after the way as the fallen part did (beneath), its new supports slid off the band by (3) and its strip and fixed-place zone already clear, refused (refuse.raised.meeting, (G3)) only where (3)'s and (4)'s bounds place no support off the band'. R7-06 (a)/E-S0's C10 adds a run repairing a dismantled span by hand after the event (viaduct and aqueduct).

issues.cell: The lock sentence's Its reach (adj l. 319–327, amended PRB7-03); C8's description (adj l. 546–552); W2's event cell and W2·C8 (adj l. 589); §4.11 Other crossings (base l. 8302–8312); §7.1's first row (base l. 10631); E-S5
issues.claim: The reach sorts a hand op on its target into 'the user locked or pinned (T10 hold)' — refused — and 'a drawn wall or a declared raised way changed by its author's new declaration (a handle drag, ..., a placeGate)'. A hand carve or T2 moved river across a drawn wall's run never T10-locked is in neither class. §7.2 locks drawn walls by default (base l. 10812, 10820), §4.11 returns an F-EDIT conflict for a locked wall in S or a new strip, §7.1 refuses new water meeting a locked wall (refuse.water); W2·C8 (C8 includes 'a drawn wall locked by its drawing') gives 'as W2·C2, no refuse.locked'. Refuse or re-trace: two builders; PRB7-03's closure fails here.
issues.required_change: Its reach adds: 'every other hand op that would re-trace, convert or remove a drawn wall or a declared raised way it does not declare — a carve or a moved river re-tracing a drawn wall's run among them — meets it as a locked one (§7.2 Drawn constraints): refused by §7.1's lock row (refuse.water, or F-EDIT's conflict), nothing written'; C8's description adds 'a carve or a moved river across a drawn run refused as across a locked one'; W2's event cell qualifies the carve and moved river 'a run neither drawn nor locked'; E-S5 adds the carve across a hand-drawn ring, refused. (Or the reverse ruling, stated in the reach, §4.11 and §7.1, and run by E-S5.)

issues.cell: (G3) at an epoch for a run a moved river or a carve re-traces: the bent group (adj l. 508–512), the fixed-place sentence (adj l. 526–528), the lock sentence (adj l. 337–339); W1's epoch re-trace (adj l. 588); §5.2's F-REDERIVE (base l. 9220)
issues.claim: V06's shiftCourse and avulsion run S1's water operator (V06 l. 2187–2198) and digCanal is a carve (V06 l. 2202–2205); the re-trace runs between the nearest unaffected towers (base l. 10927). Where the re-traced run has no lawful crossing of a standing raised way, or its water gate no point clear of a fixed-place zone in reach (a river shifting under a viaduct near the ring), the ruling gives F-REDERIVE's ladder (bent group) and walls.waited (fixed-place sentence; lock sentence). F-REDERIVE's detection and rungs name plots, ways, decks, sites and references — no wall run; and a run cannot wait for a river already moved (the river then crosses the wall with no water gate). PRB7-16's closure gave F-WALL, V06 and V07 rungs but not F-REDERIVE.
issues.required_change: Bent group: 'or, for a run a moved river re-traces, F-REDERIVE's ladder (§5.2)' -> 'or, for a run a moved river or a carve re-traces, which cannot wait, F-REDERIVE's raised-way rung (§5.2)'; the fixed-place and lock sentences' epoch clauses name the same rung for that run. New END under determinism (E-D12): F-REDERIVE's detection adds a wall run S1's water operator or a carve re-traces with no lawful crossing or no clear point for its water gate; its ladder adds 'the re-trace widened once to the next unaffected tower on each side -> the run across the water left breached (no water gate, towers standing), reported (walls.raisedCrossings)'. Scope's E-S12 adds an epoch shiftCourse fixture beside a viaduct.

issues.cell: E-D11: §5.2's F-WALL raised-way rung (adj l. 1253–1260); the lock sentence's 'F-WALL's ladder' (adj l. 337–338); the held building's ladder (adj l. 451–452); the fixed-place sentence (adj l. 527); E-S12
issues.claim: E-D11 places the raised-way rung 'before → last rung: cut a way', i.e. after re-offset with a larger radius, union-simplify, anchor by attraction, divert arterials and posterns (base l. 9203), none of which reads an under-deck strip, a fixed-place zone, Line and band's widened impassables or a held building's widened strip: a re-offset trace can pass at a pier or lay its band over a ramp, an anchor by attraction can land in a zone, and the detection's clauses do not catch either. Whether the generic rungs run first on a raised-way detection (and may stand) or it goes straight to its rung is unstated: two traces at a regeneration with a held building or raised way, and at generation on E-S12's table edit.
issues.required_change: E-D11's ladder addition -> 'for a raised-way meeting (the detection's raised-way clause) the trace takes its own ladder and none of the rungs above runs on it: the boundary re-pulled once with that raised way's under-deck strip impassable but at its lawful crossings, its fixed-place zone no crossing or anchor site and every held building's widened strip impassable -> that stage left unwalled, reported (W_RAISED_MEETING); a rung above run for another detection keeps §2.7's crossing table's rules (the pull's widened impassables, the fixed-place zone)'. E-V7-4's F-V-RAISED adds 'its rung alone runs on the raised-way detection'.

issues.cell: The lock sentence's retaining-wall clause (adj l. 341–348, amended PRB7-28) × an arch vault and a held building in it (adj l. 444–455); attack 15; E-S9 (adj l. 1075–1079)
issues.claim: A retaining wall drawn across a standing raised way 'passes beneath it as any part-0 line' (E-S9: through a support). A vault span's strip holds an arch vault chamber at grade (V04 l. 1695–1702), its strip a reservation (base l. 2565–2567), a held building possibly seated in it (V04 l. 1722–1726). Beneath's vault reading names only 'a wall's band or wall strip' and a retaining wall has none, so nothing rules its line through the chamber: kept with a wall through it (and through a held building's footprint), read open and removed (against J144's held buildings), bent like a part-0 way (row (b)), or a reservation conflict. Common on a hillside town with an aqueduct arcade.
issues.required_change: The retaining-wall clause adds after 'nothing of the raised way written': '— its line never through a vault span's under-deck strip that beneath reads vault: a drawn stroke there is bent along the deck to cross under the nearest open span or at a support (item 101 R2; a fate in bend.raised.underSpan's line), never across a span whose chamber seats a held building (by hand, with no other crossing, refuse.locked, the building the blocking entity) —'. Scope's E-S9 adds the stroke across a vault span, moved, the arch vault and its id unchanged.

issues.cell: Readers of beneath's amended vault reading (adj l. 429–444, PRB7-13; W8's absorbed runs); Block 2's lead (adj l. 614–617); R7-05 (adj l. 826–828); Part H's sweeps and the FIXes VAL-R6-03, VEL6-r6-01, VAF-R6T-04 'as written'
issues.claim: Beneath now reads a vault span open under a wall's band or strip, an absorbed record's standing run, or a way's corridor or channel laid while it read open. The homes and readers keep 'under a wall' and get no END: §2.7 (6)'s lead (base l. 2565–2567), the span rule's last sentence (base l. 2746–2748), §4.3 Lattice and costs — the crossing rule's home, 'impassable to every route' (base l. 5743), §11.1's 3-D row (base l. 16038) and GeoJSON (VAL-R6-03's text), II.7.6 (base l. 21819), V01 §1.2 and §3.17.3 (V01 l. 2467, 2473), V09 §4.20.6 (2) (V09 l. 3196–3199), V10 (VEL6-r6-01's text, T-V10-41's 'after a delete tells it vault'), V04 l. 161 and 2292, and R7-05 itself. With the intervallum or moat still under the span after the wall goes: §4.3 bars a new route Block 2 admits; the export closes the arch across the lane; V09 and V10 say vault while V04 lays no chamber. PRB7-13/PRB7-25's closure fails at the readers.
issues.required_change: R7-05: 'open for a vault span under a wall' -> 'open while a wall's band or strip, a run of an absorbed record not yet dismantled, or a way's corridor or channel laid while it read open lies across its strip ... and cites beneath for it, never restating the cases'. New ENDs replacing 'but one under a wall, read open' by 'but one §2.7's crossing table's beneath reads open' at §2.7 (6)'s lead and span rule (model), §4.3 Lattice and costs and II.7.6 (pipeline), §11.1's 3-D row and VAL-R6-03's GeoJSON words (rendering), VAF-R6T-04's row and §3.17.3 (2)–(3) (V01), §4.20.6 (2) with its disabled lines by cause (V09), VEL6-r6-01's read and T-V10-41 (V10), V04 l. 161 and §3.10.

issues.cell: Readers of Line and band and the held building's widened strip (adj l. 407–417, 446–449; PRB7-08, PRB7-01): §4.4 S5a Trace (2) (base l. 5946); V06 §3.7.6 (5) and §3.7.4 (2)'s cost field (V06 l. 1597–1600)

PRB7-08/PRB7-01's closure fails at the pull's homes.

issues.cell: Tests of amended cells: the fixed-place sentence on the epoch, founding, village and hand-success paths; W8·C1's road deck (adj l. 595); W14's kind change, village rows and W14·C9 (adj l. 601)

The fixed-place sentence's bars run at generation (E-S3, E-S1) and for the hand (G3) refusal (E-S12) only: no clause runs an epoch circuit or contraction with a water gate or anchor in a viaduct's zone (T-V6-47, E-V6-8), a founding beside a ring's water gate (E-V6-7), VS3's shore anchor beside a declared raised way's zone (T-V7-48, E-V7-1), or a hand anchor moved along its barrier with a clear point in reach. E-V6-7 (T-V6-73) adds a viaduct founded beside the CITY ring's water gate, its zone clear; E-V6-3 (T-V6-11) adds a viaduct founded across a standing absorbed run, not built, raised.waited until dismantled.
